gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the MoGo 4's 450 ISO lumens only appear in its loud Performance power mode (ProjectorCentral measured 400–404 lm with the fan at 48–52 dBA), while its 2.5-hour battery claim applies to ECO mode, which measured 151–154 lm. That is about a third of the box number and close to the 112 lm The Hook Up measured for the Nebula Capsule 3 in its 2.9-hour Eco run.
standout_why: I checked five rival pages. itechguides (MoGo 4 vs Capsule 3) says both 2.5 h figures are 'Eco Mode claims' and that ISO and ANSI can't be compared, but it never says what Eco does to brightness. Dupple ties every runtime to Eco or Power Save mode and gives no brightness for those modes. a2zcheck says the MoGo 4 Laser's 550 ISO is a 'highest-power mode' figure but gives no Eco-mode lumens. That covers part of the finding, and only for the Laser model. RTINGS' portable list page showed no figures. I couldn't open Wirecutter (the cited result) or aglena (fetch blocked / TLS error). None of the rivals I could read pairs the rated runtime with the brightness you actually get, or the rated lumens with the fan noise that comes with them.
decides: This keeps the MoGo 4 as the pick but changes what the shopper is told. Plugged in, it is about 2.5× brighter than the Capsule 3: 400 lm measured vs 161 lm. On battery at the rated 2.5 h, the gap shrinks to about 153 vs 112 lm. The Mars 3 Air managed 3 h 23 min at 128 lm. Anyone buying a mini projector mainly for battery use should expect about 110–155 lumens from any of them. The MoGo 4's real advantage is plugged-in Standard mode: 258–270 lm with the fan at 31–32 dBA. The table should put three numbers side by side: rated, quiet mode, and the battery mode behind the runtime claim.

findings.label: Measured brightness by power mode (Movie picture mode)
findings.value: Performance 404 lm / Standard 258 lm / ECO 154 lm (ISO 21118); rated 450 ISO lm
findings.source_title: XGIMI MoGo 4 1080P DLP Projector review – ProjectorCentral (Nikki Kahl, 2025-08-25)
findings.note: Measured by ProjectorCentral. Across picture modes: Performance 400–404, Standard 258–270, ECO 151–154 lm. My arithmetic: Performance is about 90% of the 450 rating and ECO about 34%.

findings.label: Measured fan noise by power mode
findings.value: Performance 48.2–52.4 dBA; Standard 31.1–32.2 dBA; ECO 31.0–31.6 dBA (rated 28 dBA)
findings.source_title: XGIMI MoGo 4 1080P DLP Projector review – ProjectorCentral
findings.note: Measured at about 3 ft from front, rear, left and right, against a 30.5 dBA room noise floor. The 450-lumen mode is the loud one.

findings.label: Battery runtime by power mode (tested)
findings.value: ECO ≈2.5 h; Standard lasted a 90-min film
findings.source_title: XGIMI MoGo 4 1080P DLP Projector review – ProjectorCentral
findings.note: Quotes: 'rated to last for up to 2.5 hours when playing video content in ECO mode'; 'In Standard power mode, the battery lasted through the new War of the Worlds film, which is 90 minutes'; 'When testing in ECO, the projector lasted around the 2.5-hour mark'. The rated runtime therefore comes with about 153 lm.

findings.label: Battery runtime, Standard mode streaming (tested)
findings.source_title: XGIMI MoGo 4 review – Expert Reviews (Stuart Andrews, 2025-06-30)
findings.note: Expert Reviews: 'In Standard mode streaming movies, the battery lasted 1hr 52mins.' The review also says Eco mode dims the picture.

findings.label: Price, XGIMI US store
findings.value: $479.00 (compare-at $599); MoGo 4 + PowerBase Stand $519; PowerBase Stand alone $129

findings.label: Price and rated brightness, XGIMI US store
findings.value: $669.00; 550 ISO lm; 'up to 2.5 hours of playtime'
findings.note: Same 2.5 h claim as the LED model. I found no measured ECO-mode lumens for the Laser (see unsourced).

findings.label: Measured brightness plugged in vs Eco, and battery runtime
findings.value: 161 ANSI lm plugged in; 112 lm in Eco; 2 h 53 min on the internal battery at 112 lm; 7 h 14 min with a 20,000 mAh power bank
findings.source_title: Ultimate Portable Projector Comparison – 2024 Update – The Hook Up (2024-09-12)
findings.note: Average of 9 readings on a full-white screen. 161 lm is about 80% of Nebula's 200 ANSI claim. The Hook Up tested the 200-ANSI LED Capsule 3 in 2024, which may be the Android TV version rather than the Google TV unit sold now; same light engine and rating, but a different variant.

findings.label: Measured brightness and battery runtime
findings.value: 450 ANSI lm at full brightness (rated 400); 203 lm in Eco; 3 h 23 min on battery at 128 lm
findings.source_title: Ultimate Portable Projector Comparison – 2024 Update – The Hook Up
findings.note: The page gives 203 lm for Eco and 128 lm for the runtime run without explaining the difference; the runtime run used a lower setting. Nebula claims 2.5 h.

findings.label: Normalised table footnote
findings.value: Lumens at the rated battery runtime: MoGo 4 ≈153 lm (2.5 h, ECO); Capsule 3 112 lm (2 h 53 min, Eco); Mars 3 Air 128 lm (3 h 23 min). Plugged-in maximum: 404 / 161 / 450 lm.
findings.source_title: ProjectorCentral MoGo 4 review + The Hook Up 2024 portable comparison (https://www.thesmarthomehookup.com/test_install/?p=6317)
findings.note: Combines the two measured sources above. ISO 21118 (ProjectorCentral) and nine-point ANSI (The Hook Up) are different methods, so differences of a few percent between products mean little. The roughly 2.5× plugged-in gap between MoGo 4 and Capsule 3 shrinks to about 1.4× on battery.
